bullets.title: October CPI hotter than expected; 50bp December hike firmly on table
bullets.body: Core CPI printed +0.296–0.30% MoM vs. ~0.20% consensus, the third consecutive hot print; supercore came in at +0.40% vs. 0.27% consensus. Core PCE is nowcasting ~0.33–0.35% for October. Fed Governor Waller explicitly flagged openness to 50bp in December if inflation stays at this level, though analysts broadly expect 25bp in December/January as the base case. 56–59% of CPI categories are rising >3% YoY, the highest breadth since mid-2023.

bullets.title: Services inflation and housing disinflation reversal are the structural sticking points
bullets.body: OER posted +0.32% MoM, market rents are bouncing back after prior disinflation, and core services ex-housing remain sticky. Super core services rose +0.40% MoM. Morgan Stanley notes the main surprise was the 'lack of progress on services,' and multiple desks flag services as the greatest obstacle to returning to 2%.

bullets.title: Fed rate cycle could reach 5.25–6.25%; neutral rate drifting higher
bullets.body: 22V Research flags that prior Fed tightening cycles averaged 10 hikes (range 6–17); at the low end (6 hikes) the terminal rate hits 5.25%, at the average (10 hikes) it reaches 6.25% — the Fed has raised once so far. JPM separately argues neutral rates are drifting higher driven by equilibrium pressures from the capex boom funding needs, with tight labor markets limiting disinflation cushions from unit labor costs.

bullets.title: Tape opens on defense: NDX futures -100bps after Monday's +3.4% rally; CTA selling pressure
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures were up ~0.72% pre-CPI but quickly faced pressure post-print; 2Y yields rose 13bps, 10Y +5–9bps. GS estimates CTAs will sell ~$28B in S&P over the next week. SpotGamma flags SPX 7600 as upside resistance and 7200 as the washout level. Long/short community is already at 1st-percentile net leverage, limiting incremental downside acceleration.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure sees heavy selling; zero dip-buying; defensive rotation into building products
bullets.body: Oppenheimer desk reports a 2–3:1 sell-to-buy ratio last week with momentum picking up Tuesday; AI infrastructure names seeing 'almost zero dip buying.' E&P and midstream also seeing significant outflows. Building products attracting buyers on rate-move and anti-AI rotation themes. Hedge funds had flipped to large net buyers of US equities Monday with 5% bounce in nets, but that move is unwinding.

bullets.title: SOX P/E at historical trough (13.4x); semis down 30% from June peak — retest of 8,000–8,300 possible
bullets.body: MS reports SOX forward P/E fell from 26.3x (June) to 13.4x, matching the historical downturn median and -1 std dev vs. the post-2011 average of 18.6x. Multiple desks flag that SOX likely needs to retest the April breakout level (8,000–8,300), implying another 12–15% downside before a durable advance. BofA removed LRCX, MU, and NVDA from its US 1 List.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO launches at $70–78/share (~$1.18–1.32T valuation); $26B concurrent from NVDA, AMD, GOOGL, MSFT, AVGO
bullets.body: Anthropic is raising ~$64B in its IPO (825M shares, 97% primary) with an additional $26B concurrent private placement from Google, NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC. The valuation of $1.18–1.32T (pre-money, fully diluted) is 35–55% below prior $1.5–2T expectations. Pricing is expected November 18 post-close, trading begins November 19. IPO implies 8.1–9.1x 2027E EV/revenue.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO investigation drives ~25% bear-case discount; export controls risk back on the table
bullets.body: Multiple desks reporting on a board-led investigation into Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset who facilitated $7.5B+ chip shipments to China since 2023. Yorkville Ives values NVDA 25–30% lower if Huang is removed (15% probability assigned). The White House is also reconsidering tightening export controls on advanced AI chips in the wake of the scandal. Citi trimmed NVDA PT 10% to $285 but maintains Buy; NVDA underperformed SOX by ~11% Monday.

bullets.title: AI capex boom is Stage 1 (demand shock), not Stage 2 (productivity realization); macro implications hawkish
bullets.body: JPM argues the productivity surge is 50% capital deepening and only ~30% true TFP growth; TFP has stalled over the past year despite the AI narrative. US tech capex skyrocketed 30% YoY; global capex +7% annualized since early 2025. Most value from the $1.2T hyperscaler capex boom flows to Asian manufacturers, not US businesses. The result: cyclical hiring rebound, sticky inflation, and structurally higher neutral rates.

bullets.title: AI capex crowding out buybacks; hyperscalers (GOOGL, AMZN) showing FCF strain and rising debt
bullets.body: Capex now accounts for 41% of S&P 500 total cash usage — more than double any other category — while net buybacks fell to 14% of cash use. 3Q marks the first quarter since 2021 where capex exceeded total shareholder cash returns. GOOGL and AMZN are the most strained, with FCF-to-total-debt ratios near zero; GOOGL conducted two equity offerings in June to fund AI infrastructure.

bullets.title: Texas data-center tax incentive repeal threat adds to DC buildout durability concerns
bullets.body: 22V flags that 24 of 1,173 day-one Texas legislative filings (2%) target data centers, with repeal of sales tax exemptions as consensus legislation across multiple bill variants. GEV's PORTS Pike project (~8% of Power and Electrification backlog) faces separate financing risk. MS shifted ~5GW of US data center projects from 2028 to 2029 post-midterms, cutting global additions growth from 21% to 9% in 2028.

bullets.title: H-1B visa crackdown hits IT consulting: IBM ends sponsorship; ACN, CTSH, INFY move to lows
bullets.body: IBM is ending visa and green card sponsorship for its Consulting division. VP Vance suspended Microsoft's access to the PERM program over alleged H-1B abuse; Labor Secretary also suspended Adobe from PERM. IT consulting stocks including ACN, CTSH, and INFY moved to session lows following the White House press conference.

bullets.title: Microsoft pushes Trump to abandon Chinese optical transceiver ban; COHR, LITE down 5–8%
bullets.body: Microsoft is pressing the Trump administration to abandon a planned ban on Chinese optical transceivers. COHR and LITE fell 5–8% in pre-market on the news, as the ban would have been a potential US sourcing tailwind for domestic optical component makers.

bullets.title: Internet sector outperforms: AMZN +8%, GOOGL +2% vs NDX -5%; sector trades at compressed multiples
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley rates Internet as Attractive: the sector gained +4% vs SPX/NDX at -3/-5%. AMZN and GOOGL led at +8%/+2%, trading at 20x/15x forward 2026 EPS despite EPS estimates down 27%/40% vs TTM. APP surged +71%, ABNB +16%; META declined 1% and SNAP fell 7%.

bullets.title: NFIB small business: price-hike intentions at highest since July 2022; uncertainty falling
bullets.body: October NFIB small business optimism was 97.8 (down 0.1pt YoY but above 6-month average). Uncertainty fell 6pts to 84, the first sizable decline in 2026. Hiring intentions and unfilled job openings both rose, but price hike intentions reached the highest level since July 2022 — consistent with sticky services inflation.

bullets.title: Post-midterm regime: bearish Quad 4 setup with flattening curve; setup resembles falling growth/falling inflation
bullets.body: Multiple desks flag the macro setup as deteriorating: 2Y up 13bps, 10Y up 5bps post-CPI, with the curve bear-flattening signaling growth deceleration into 2027. Hedgeye's Quad 4 (falling growth, falling inflation) framing is being cited as the worst macro environment for equities. Positioning is heavily cleaned out — JPM institutional sentiment below -2 std dev — but showing signs of bottoming.

bullets.title: TSMC October revenue +59.7% YoY; memory NAND spot prices -20% in 2 weeks — diverging AI supply chain
bullets.body: TSMC's October revenue growth of +59.7% YoY confirms AI/leading-edge chip demand remains robust. However, NAND spot prices fell ~20% in 2 weeks (512Gb TLC wafers at $15, ~27–29% below March peak) as buyers substitute cheaper DIMMs and QLC SSDs for KV-cache; no near-term floor identified. Memory represents ~60% of AI server BOM, making this a meaningful margin/mix headwind.

bullets.title: Akamai raises $2.2B in converts; Dropbox $1.1B — tech convert issuance picking up
bullets.body: Akamai priced $2.2B in convertible senior notes (split $1.1B due 2028 / $1.1B due 2031 at 1.00%) and Dropbox priced a $1.1B convertible offering. Tech convert supply is a marginal headwind to equity as dealers hedge delta.

bullets.title: JPM post-midterm bank view: constructive but selective; prefers exchanges, info services, insurance brokers
bullets.body: JPM remains constructive on financials overall but cautious near-term on large-cap banks, caught between higher rates (NII/trading tailwind) and weaker capital markets if AI capex is reassessed. SoftBank took a $3.7B writedown on AI data-center power equipment. Data-center slowdown risks are more fee-pool than credit-loss for banks; financing runs through private credit and project finance, not bank balance sheets.

bullets.title: VIX short call in play; VIX ~16 is the target before it's faded
bullets.body: 22V maintains a VIX short call, targeting ~16 (another ~4% lower for low-vol strategies). The caveat is unforeseen AI news (e.g., the NVDA CEO situation) that could move the target. With gross leverage at the 26th percentile and net at the 1st percentile, the long/short community is unlikely to accelerate downside from here.
